$comment: G7. Paths an automated branch may not touch: they define what the system may do and what it may read. An automation that can edit its own limits has none. This list is the single home; gate-protected-paths.sh checks that the fenced block under '## G7 — Protected paths' in docs/gate-requirements.md still says exactly the same thing, so the rule and its documentation cannot drift apart.
$comment_branch_prefixes: A branch prefix is a name the editor chooses, so it can only INCRIMINATE. Matching one is an admission and fails; not matching one proves nothing and is never an exculpation. Measured on PR #72: an agent raised MAX_TREE_BYTES inside scripts/gates/** on a branch it had itself named `loop/...`, and this gate passed it green.

automation_commit_markers.$comment: Signals in the COMMIT RANGE rather than in the branch name. An agent does not type these; its harness writes them. They are still not proof of a human when absent - nothing available at gate time is - so they are read in one direction only, exactly like the prefix above.
